_note: The regression gate. Every prompt change is scored against this before merge; a change that does not improve the score is not merged. Cases were hand-verified during Phase 0 — the expected values are what a careful human concluded from the cited evidence, not what any model produced. Add cases as new failure modes are discovered; never edit an expected value to make a run pass.

cases.why: Manufacturer spec states Wi-Fi and Bluetooth not supported; no FCC intentional-radiator grant while siblings have them.
Has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a phone app, but VIOFO operates no cloud service — the app is peer-to-peer to the camera's own AP.
cases.trap: Pattern-matching on 'has Wi-Fi and an app' yields D2. There must be a vendor cloud for the cloud to be optional. Failing this case means the D1/D2 boundary is not understood.

cases.why: The door opens from the wall button and RF remote with no network. Chamberlain's revocation of third-party API access is vendor conduct, scored at vendor_risk 3, not a tier input.
cases.trap: The vendor's behaviour is genuinely hostile and invites a REJECT. Publishing REJECT sends a reader hunting for a problem they will not find. Tier describes the device; vendor_risk describes the vendor.

cases.why: No local storage exists at any price, and reviewing recorded video requires a subscription. Core function of a video doorbell includes seeing who was there.
cases.trap: Live view works without a subscription, which reads as 'partially offline' and tempts a D2. The test is whether the device can record to anything the owner controls. It cannot.

cases.why: Whether an eWeLink account is mandatory as sold is unresolved, and that single fact is the difference between D3 and D2.
cases.trap: A maintained Tasmota path is easy to find and makes D3 feel obvious. The correct answer is to hold the record. Any run that publishes a tier here has failed, regardless of which tier it picked.

cases.why: WeatherLink Cloud exists and is optional; console holds the full database locally. Arguably D1 if the sensor link proves to be open — flagging that in open_questions is the correct behaviour, not picking silently.
Bluetooth and an OMRON cloud exist but the manual documents standalone use and onboard storage. Account is app-only.
USB-only with no network interface. Firmware can still be pushed from the host computer, which is a real caveat but not a radio — D0 stands and the caveat belongs in open_questions.
USB-only per manufacturer spec page; product page shows Discontinued. Must be published with discontinued status, not dropped.
Manufacturer spec states 'WiFi: No' and 'RedLINK: No'; Resideo holds grants only for its connected thermostats.
Manufacturer spec enumerates every input; no network interface of any kind appears.
Sold in the manufacturer's explicitly non-cellular line; the grantee that files Browning's authorizations holds a cellular grant only for the Command X.
Electromechanical clock motor and physical trippers. The floor of the scale.

Mechanical dial controls, no connectivity listed. Whether the timer is a true cam timer or an electronic timer behind a dial is unresolved and does not change the tier — recording that uncertainty is correct behaviour.
Obviously radio-free, but the manufacturer page timed out and the record rests on two Class B sources. The correct behaviour is to publish under the two-Class-B rule and say so, not to claim Class A.

Three fetches failed (manufacturer domain, two distributors) before ACP Inc was identified as the actual manufacturer. The evidence exists but is not at the first URL — giving up early yields a wrong insufficient_evidence.
ONVIF/RTSP to an owner-run NVR, local detection, no subscription — but Reolink operates a cloud and an app, so D2.
cases.trap: A camera that can be run entirely on a LAN invites D1. D1 requires the vendor to operate no cloud for the device at all; 'I can block it at the firewall' is not a tier property, it is a property of the owner's network. Compare the VIOFO A139, which is genuinely D1 because no VIOFO cloud exists.

cases.why: FCC grants for both units cover DECT only, no WiFi or Bluetooth. A point-to-point link between two units the owner holds, with no vendor service of any kind.
cases.trap: Tempting to call D0 because it feels like a dumb appliance — but it has an intentional radiator, so D1 is correct. Equally, the presence of a radio does not push it to D2.

cases.why: No ports, no radio, solar/battery. Exam approval independently certifies the absence of communication capability.
